_comment: LOCAL gold-set template (W3.4). Same format as docs/gold-set-template.json — read by src/pipeline/calibration.py (load_gold_set) — but for service-area businesses. Replace the skeleton items with 25-40 REAL answers pulled from a local proxy run, hand-labeled by a HUMAN (never by a model; independence is the entire point). Run: python -m src.cli calibrate data/local_gold.json
_why_a_separate_file: Never mix ICPs in one gold set. The consumer figures (96/88/93) were measured on Oura and Fort; a blended file would produce an agreement number that describes neither ICP. Local calibrates separately and reports separately.
_procedure: 1. Run a real local audit (a trade template from data/queries_<trade>.json, rendered with a real city + brand, engines including google_ai_overviews WITH a location).

2. Export the answers (python -m src.cli report <run_id>, or docs/answers.md style) and paste real answer text into the items below. Never write synthetic answers - the judge is being measured against reality.
3. Fill the fact_sheet field from that business's docs/fact-sheet-template-local.md sheet. Only items WITH a fact sheet count toward flag precision/recall.
4. Label present/prominence/framing per brand, and expected_flags per item, BY HAND.
5. Freeze the file. Split into a tune subset and a held-out subset; report only on held-out; draw any judge-prompt few-shot examples ONLY from tune.
6. Calibration uses the held-constant API judge with isolated_cache() - NEVER the shared Supabase cache, and NEVER subscription/Opus (prejudge) verdicts. Those are dev-only.

_local_flag_types.wrong_hours: opening hours, days, emergency / same-day / 24-7 availability
_local_flag_types.wrong_service_area: which towns, neighborhoods, counties or radius they cover
_local_flag_types.wrong_contact: phone number or street address (format differences are AGREEMENT, not a flag)
_local_flag_types.licensing: licence, bond, insurance or certification status
_local_flag_types._also_available: wrong_pricing, missing_or_invented_feature, competitor_confusion, identity, stale - a local business still has services and prices

_labeling_traps_specific_to_local: A same-named business in another metro is the #1 local confusion - label it identity, not competitor_confusion, when the answer describes the WRONG business under the client's name.
'Open 24/7' against a sheet that says 'No after-hours service' is wrong_hours. 'Call for availability' with no stated hours is NOT a flag - no value was asserted.
An AI naming the client's own city as served is AGREEMENT. Only a town the sheet's service-area line contradicts is wrong_service_area.
An omission is never a flag - an AI failing to mention the emergency line is a VISIBILITY finding, not an accuracy one.

Local answers frequently name businesses that do not exist or have closed. If the CLIENT is described accurately, that is not a client accuracy flag - it is a competitor-set problem, noted separately.
